info.description: The open fact layer for commercial real estate AI agents: deterministic CRE calculators with audit trails, canonical FactLot IDs, and cited-fact validation. Call these operations instead of doing lease, CAM, rent, loan, or return math yourself. This document is the curated Custom GPT Actions subset: 26 of the 41 operations (Actions accept at most 30). Every tool is in the OpenAPI 3.1 document (/openapi.json) and over MCP (/mcp); /openapi-3.0.json?operations=all is the complete OpenAPI 3.0 document.

post.description: Build a base-rent schedule from commencement date, term, area, starting $/SF/yr, escalations (percent or fixed $/SF), and abated months. Lease months run from the commencement day-of-month with no calendar proration (warns when commencement is mid-month). Returns rent steps, totals, expiration date, and a calculation trace. Optional unit (kw, mw, unit, acre, key, room, space) relabels area and $/SF for data-center, ground, yard, residential, hotel, or parking leases without changing any number. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.rent_schedule@1 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

post.description: Rank 2–20 lease proposals with different terms, sizes, free rent, TI, concessions, and operating-expense structures (gross, NNN, base year, expense stop, with opex growth) on one discounted $/SF/yr basis, per rentable or usable SF (load factor): effective occupancy cost (tenant perspective) or discounted net effective rent after landlord-borne opex and optional pre-commencement downtime (landlord perspective). Cash flows monthly in advance at annual rate ÷ 12; warns when the usable-SF ranking differs and when terms differ. schedule.unit (kw, mw, unit, acre, key, room, space, the same for every proposal) ranks per kW, MW, unit, acre, key, room, or space instead of per SF. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.compare_proposals@2 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

post.description: Analyze an apartment rent roll (up to 5,000 units with status occupied, notice, vacant, model, or down; market and lease rent per month; lease dates; concessions as weeks free, months free, or dollars): gross potential rent, vacancy, non-revenue units, loss to lease, concessions amortised straight-line over each lease term, effective rent income, physical and economic occupancy, effective rent per unit and per SF, a lease expiration schedule by month, and a per-unit-type summary. Single-lease mode (lease instead of units) returns the effective monthly rent after a weeks-free or months-free concession. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.multifamily_rent_roll@1 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

sf.description: Unit square feet. Needed for per-SF figures.

lease_rent.description: Contract (lease) rent per month, USD, before concessions. Required for occupied and notice units; ignored for vacant, model, and down units.

lease_end.description: Lease end date (last day), YYYY-MM-DD. A lease that ended before as_of is month-to-month.

oneOf.description: A dollar concession for the whole lease.

post.description: Reconcile a tenant's annual CAM charge: exclusions, occupancy gross-up of variable expenses, pro rata share, controllable-expense caps (compounding_from_base, simple_from_base, year_over_year), an admin fee (before or after the cap, inside or outside it, with per-line exclusions), base year or expense stop, partial-year occupancy (move-in/move-out prorates share, cap, and base by days), and estimates paid. Returns balance due and a full trace with order-of-operations warnings. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.cam_reconciliation@2 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

category.description: Expense line as named in the operating statement, e.g. "janitorial".

amount.description: Building-level actual expense for the year, USD.

controllable.description: Subject to the cap. Taxes, insurance, and utilities are typically uncontrollable.

recoverable.description: Excluded expenses (capital items, landlord-only costs) are dropped entirely.

variable.description: Varies with occupancy, so eligible for gross-up (janitorial, utilities, management fee).

admin_fee_applies.description: Included in the admin_fee base. Set false for lines the lease excludes from the fee (often taxes, insurance, utilities, or a management fee already charged).

expenses.description: Building operating expense lines for the year.

gross_up.description: Gross up variable expenses to the target occupancy when actual occupancy is lower. Omit if the lease has no gross-up.

actual_occupancy.description: Average occupancy for the year, e.g. 0.82.

target_occupancy.description: Gross-up occupancy stated in the lease (commonly 0.95 or 1.0).

structure.description: Expense structure from the lease. Default: net.

oneOf.description: Tenant pays its full share of recoverable expenses (NNN / net).

base_year_expenses.description: Total building recoverable expenses in the base year, already grossed up, USD.

oneOf.description: Tenant pays its share of the excess over base-year expenses.

stop_amount.description: Building-level expense stop, USD per year.

oneOf.description: Tenant pays its share of the excess over a fixed expense stop.

cap.description: Cap on the tenant's share of controllable expenses. Omit if the lease has no cap.

method.description: compounding_from_base: reference × (1+rate)^years (often called cumulative, compounding). simple_from_base: reference × (1 + rate × years) (cumulative, non-compounding). year_over_year: prior year's capped amount × (1+rate) (non-cumulative). Map the lease language to one of these explicitly.

rate.description: Annual cap as a decimal, e.g. 0.05.

reference_amount.description: Tenant's share of controllable expenses in the reference year: the base year for *_from_base, or the prior year's capped amount for year_over_year, USD.

years_elapsed.description: Years since the base year (required for `*_from_base`).

admin_fee.description: Administrative fee the lease adds to the tenant's share. Omit if the lease has none.

rate.description: Administrative or management fee as a decimal of the fee base, e.g. 0.15 for 15%. The base is the tenant's share of recoverable lines with admin_fee_applies (after gross-up).

applied.description: Fee on controllable lines computed on the tenant's share before the cap (before_cap) or on the capped amount (after_cap). Fees on uncontrollable lines are never capped. Irrelevant without a cap.

capped.description: True when the fee on controllable lines counts toward the controllable cap (controllable share plus fee may not exceed the cap limit); false adds it outside the cap.

occupancy.description: Partial-year occupancy: the tenant's share, cap limit, and base-year or stop deduction are prorated by occupied days ÷ period days (both inclusive), so a full-year cap and base are not applied to a part year. Omit for a full year.

move_in_date.description: Date the tenant's share starts within the reconciliation period, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to period_start_date.

move_out_date.description: Last day of the tenant's share within the period, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to period_end_date.

period_start_date.description: First day of the reconciliation period, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to January 1 of year; set it for a lease year.

period_end_date.description: Last day of the reconciliation period, YYYY-MM-DD (at most 366 days after the start). Defaults to December 31 of year.

estimates_paid.description: Estimated CAM payments the tenant made during the year, USD (total for the year, not monthly).

until_irr.description: LP IRR hurdle (annual, as calc_irr annualizes) that ends this tier, e.g. 0.12.

promote.description: Share of each dollar in this tier paid to the GP as promote, e.g. 0.2 for an 80/20 split; the rest goes to the investors pro rata to capital.

post.description: Check values YOU extracted from a document against its text, deterministically; FactLot runs no model. Send the pages as text and one candidate per value: {predicate, value, quote, page}. Each candidate is checked in order: (1) the value's shape (Ingest predicates such as lease.expiration_date YYYY-MM-DD, lease.pro_rata_share in (0, 1], ordered lease.base_rent_schedule steps; any other dotted predicate needs a non-empty value); (2) the quote, at least 12 characters, is on the cited page, where only whitespace, line breaks, letter case and typographic quotes and dashes may differ (a word hyphenated across a line must keep its hyphen; a quote found on exactly one other page is accepted with the page corrected); (3) every number, date and party name in the value is written in the quote, in any common form: 1250000 matches "$1,250,000.00", 0.03 matches "3%" or "three percent", 2031-06-30 matches "June 30, 2031" or "6/30/2031"; text the lease states as written (a prohibited use, a carve-out, a protected use) is written in it as words, ignoring case, punctuation and line breaks; (4) a confidence you give below 0.8 holds it for review; (5) every other part of the value must be confirmed by the quote too: a true/false value, an enum or a summary not written in the quote holds the candidate for review, named in the reason. Verified means every part of the value was found in the quote. Returns verified (FactLot facts: method extracted, citing document_id, page, quote and character span, plus which value parts were checked and as what), needs_review (the quote is on the page but does not state the value: check consistency; low confidence: confidence; a part FactLot cannot confirm from the quote, such as a boolean: coverage) and rejected (wrong shape; quote missing, too short, or on several pages), each with a reason to act on. Not checked: meaning (a quote stating the number in another context passes), and whether the pages came from the file whose sha256 you give.

post.description: Current-state lease abstract from a lease and its amendments, with amendment precedence, as of as_of. Give each document's pages with the candidates you extracted (checked exactly as doc_verify_facts checks them), or the facts doc_verify_facts already returned for it (without pages only the value against its quote is rechecked, marked quote_on_page: false). Documents may come in any order: give the lease role original and each amendment role amendment with its effective_date (without a role the lease is inferred only when that is unambiguous, otherwise it is an input error; two or more amendments need effective dates). The original applies first, then amendments by effective_date; a later document's value for a predicate controls, and the earlier one moves to history and is linked through supersedes. An amendment effective after as_of is pending: its values are listed under pending and pending_facts with a warning and do not control. A rent schedule restated from a later date keeps the earlier steps before it (carried_forward). Each field gives its value, the controlling document, page, quote and fact, the superseded history, conflicts (two different values from one document, or from two documents of the same rank), pending values and open_items (a candidate for that predicate in the controlling or a later document that needs review or was rejected, so the value may not be final).
